segments.text: Let me tell you a secret.
We are going to call it the silent rehearsal.
This is a method to speak English fluently and understand native speakers quickly.
But
wait.
Your teacher at school told you to practice speaking with a partner, right?
Or to find a native speaker to talk to?
That is the old way.
That is why you feel stuck and nervous when you open your mouth.
Nobody talks about this, but you actually don't need another person to practice.
You are the only person you need.
By the end of this video, you will
know exactly how to use your alone time to build confidence.
You will sound better and think faster in English.
You will stop freezing in conversations.
I
have a friend.
His name is Marco.
Marco is just like you.
He knows grammar.
He knows many words.
But he couldn't speak fast.
He was shy.
He didn't have any foreign friends.
He started using this secret method alone in his room.
He did it every day.
After 30 days, he talked to an American tourist.
He was surprised.
He spoke clearly.
He didn't feel nervous.
The tourist said, "Your English is great."
It really works.
So, here is the plan.
We will do three things.
One, stop translating.
Two, speak the news.
Three, act like a spy.
Are you ready?
Let's go.
Here is the first big mistake.
When you study, you see a word.
You translate it in your head.
For example, you see apple.
You think apple.
Then you speak.
That takes too much time.
This is why you speak slowly.
The secret is to connect words to feelings and pictures.
Let's do a test.
Close your eyes.
Think about your morning.
Don't say morning.
See the sun in your eyes.
Feel the warm coffee in your hands.
Hear the sound of a shower.
Now your brain has a picture.
The word coffee is right there.
You don't need to translate.
You just need to name the picture.
Here is your new homework.
Every day when you are alone, look at things and describe them in your head.
For 5 minutes, just look around your room.
Say it in your head.
The wall is white.
My phone is on the table.
The window is big.
Don't think in your first language.
Try to see pictures.
This helps you think faster.
That was easy, but point two is the real game changer for your mouth muscles.
Point two, speak the news, shadowing.
Okay, so you think in pictures. Good, but your mouth is still lazy.
You need to make your mouth move. You need to make sounds.
Here is the secret.
You will be a reporter. You will copy the
news.
You don't need a partner for this.
You just need a video or an audio clip.
Find a short video in English, maybe an interview, maybe a news story, just 30 seconds.
Listen to one sentence, then pause the video.
Say the sentence exactly like the speaker.
Try to copy the rhythm.
Try to copy the feeling.
Are they happy? Are they serious?
Copy them.
For example, if they say, "The weather is beautiful today."
You say it.
Say it loud. Don't whisper.
Move your mouth a lot. Over exaggerate.
Do this three times for the same sentence.
This is called shadowing.
You are copying the native speaker's music.
This trains your tongue.
You will find it tiring at first.
That is good. It means you are working.
Do this for 5 minutes a day.
You will feel your mouth getting stronger.
Your pronunciation will get better.
But wait, speaking is only half the story.
The next point is the most fun part. It's about listening to yourself.
Point three, the tape recorder trick.
Recording.
This is the part nobody wants to do.
But this is the biggest secret.
When you are alone, you are your best teacher.
How?
You need to listen to yourself.
Most students don't know what they sound like.
They think they sound good, but they say words wrong.
Or they think they sound bad, but actually they sound good.
So, do this.
Take your phone.
Open the voice recorder.
Today, we practice point two again.
You record yourself saying your 30-second new sentence.
Then play it back.
Listen to yourself.
Compare it to the native speaker.
Did you say beautiful or beautiful?
Listen closely.
This is a magic moment.
Usually your teacher tells you you are wrong.
But now, you hear it yourself.
You can fix it.
You don't need a teacher for the small things.
Don't judge yourself.
Be curious.
Say, "Oh, I didn't say the T sound."
Then record again.
Try to make it better.
Nobody hears this tape but you.
It is your private laboratory.
This is how you become independent.
Now, we have the tools, but how do you have a real conversation if you are scared?
The last point tells you exactly what to do.
Point four, the interrogation method.
Listen and repeat.
Let me tell you another secret.
A conversation is not just about you. A conversation is about listening and reacting.
If you are alone, you can practice this with
movies.
Watch a scene, pause before the actor answers.
You are the detective.
You are interrogating the suspect.
You see a man on screen. He asks a question.
Where did you go last night?
You pause.
You are the suspect now.
You must answer.
Say your answer out loud.
I went to the library.
Then, play the video.
Hear the actor's answer.
Did you say the same?
Did you use different words?
Does your answer make sense?
This is great because you practice reacting and responding under pressure.
You learn how to answer questions fast.
It trains your brain to find the right word immediately. You don't wait for a partner.
